Purpose and exclusions

A2D service actor routes merchant/trainer/dialogue/quest roles without owning character records.

Never bypass the declared rule owner, mutate an authored definition at runtime, trust a client completion claim, or infer a compiled implementation from this page.

Creation and configuration

  1. Build native service Actor and BP_NPC_Mara. Add the relevant native domain components and assign vendor definition11; attach dialogue/quest links15 and trainer services20 only when implemented.
  2. Set NPCId/display name/appearance on each placed service instance. Reuse the native role composition for Tovin rather than copying inventory/quest variables into a second NPC.
  3. Bind UMG screens to the current interaction context and player-owned model. On actor destruction, travel or range loss close context, unbind and clear focus without inventing a refund.

Required sequence: create native prerequisites -> actual build -> child/data creation -> configure -> assign to listed consumer -> save -> run named fixture. A compiled shell without its consumer assignment is not feature completion.

Project custom contracts are not engine/plugin nodes. A read-only asset participates through its consumer; it does not inherit that consumer’s mutation methods. Backend endpoint pages label transport proposals explicitly.

Lifecycle and cleanup

  1. Construct with only safe defaults; no service calls or world scans from construction scripts.
  2. Inject current owner/definition/session and subscribe once after readiness. Possession and replicated state may arrive in either order; guard initialization.
  3. Accept only permitted commands under current identity/epoch; keep local UI/cosmetic prediction separate from committed state.
  4. After server/backend result apply only matching request generation and nonstale revision; late reply to old body does not mutate new body.
  5. On death, transfer, disconnect, restart or teardown cancel transient work, clear input/timers, unbind delegates and release weak observers. Durable receipts remain authoritative.
  6. On reconnect create fresh runtime objects from current committed snapshot; never deserialize old Actor/widget pointers or rerun initial grants.

Concrete player-to-authority flow

Participation in Currency, merchants, stock, buyback and repairs. Rule owner: URPGMerchantComponent. This asset’s role is A2D service actor routes merchant/trainer/dialogue/quest roles without owning character records.

  1. Player talks to NPC_Mara; interaction server checks range/LOS and returns a vendor context and versioned offers.
  2. Buy UI requests a quote for a bounded quantity. Backend/zone price rules include catalog, stock and approved reputation modifiers; client displayed total is not authority.
  3. On confirm, lock wallet/inventory/vendor-stock/quote rows in a consistent order, repeat eligibility and capacity checks, and either apply all deltas or reject all.
  4. Selling transfers the exact item/quantity out and creates a seller-scoped buyback entry in the same transaction that credits currency; do not reroll or recreate the sold gear.
  5. Buyback consumes that entry and returns the same gear UUID, charging the stored price under the policy. Repairs update specific owned durability values and wallet together.
  6. Restock uses server time and a durable generation so restart cannot multiply stock. Results update UMG from committed revisions; stale quotes are refreshed explicitly.

Named fixture and acceptance

Fixture: L_Rillmere / NPC_Mara / Offer_Draught / Buyback_A. Configure this asset at its first phase and run the linked phase recipe. Actual result: not run in Unreal/backend during documentation generation.

Stimulus / expected result
Two clients buy last stock -> one Purchased, one OutOfStock; only winner pays.
Insufficient funds or space -> unchanged wallet, inventory and stock.
Price changes after quote -> StaleQuote under strict quote-version policy; ask player to reconfirm.
Sell request uses replaced UUID -> StaleItem; no wrong gear sold.

Record expected/observed separately. Reopen the concrete map consumer; inspect authoritative state, stable IDs/revisions and UI. Static link checks cannot satisfy this gameplay test.

Common mistakes and staged limits

Do not duplicate a native rule in Blueprint, assume a planned type is compiled, or keep callbacks/owners valid after world or session replacement.

Do not build later references as empty shells in an earlier phase. Source-derived art rows remain blocked by the missing ZIP; plugin API bindings remain blocked by installed-source verification. Placeholder visuals and proposed tuning are explicitly not production proof.
